description: First Bulgarian Empire (681–1018) founded when Asparuh's Bulgars crossed the Danube and established a state mixing Bulgar nomadic aristocracy with Slavic peasant population; Boris I's conversion to Christianity (864) established Bulgaria in the Byzantine cultural orbit while Simeon I's military campaigns made Bulgaria the dominant Balkan power and his Preslav court pioneered Slavonic literary culture in Cyrillic script.

temporal.notes: Stub: dates from GeoJSON basemap years 1000–1400

lifecycle_phases.description: Asparuh's Bulgars cross Danube and defeat Byzantine Emperor Constantine IV (681); first Bulgar-Slavic confederation established south of the Danube
Krum Khan defeats Byzantine army and kills Emperor Nikephoros I (811); Bulgaria extends to Adriatic and Aegean coasts; Preslav becomes capital
Boris I converts to Orthodox Christianity (864); Simeon I defeats Byzantium multiple times and titles himself 'Caesar of the Bulgarians and Romans'
Macedonian Byzantine dynasty's military revival; Basil II defeats Bulgaria at Kleidion (1014) and blinds 15,000 prisoners; Bulgaria absorbed into Byzantine Empire (1018)

rise_factors.description: Bulgar cavalry mobility combined with Slavic infantry to create a combined force that repeatedly defeated the heavier Byzantine professional army in Balkan terrain
Balkan mountain ranges, Stara Planina, Rhodopes, provided defensive depth against Byzantine campaigns from Constantinople

decline_factors.description: Byzantine Macedonian dynasty's military recovery under Nikephoros II and Basil II reversed Bulgar military advantage through superior organisation and siege technology
